passage:
At the start of the year, Class 807 made a class promise. Instead of rules written by the teacher, students wrote what kind of class they wanted.
They wrote: listen when others speak, return borrowed things, help classmates who are absent, and do not laugh at mistakes.
The teacher printed the promise and put it on the wall. When problems happened, she pointed to it and asked, "Which promise can help us now"
Because students had written the words themselves, the promise felt different from normal rules.
By the end of the year, the paper was old and the corners were bent. But the class still remembered it. Shared words can guide people when they are taken seriously.
